source_text: Cogimur quaedam identidem iterare, ut cohaerentia eis confirmemus. dominum et hic retributorem utriusque meriti dicimus circumferri ab apostolo, aut creatorem aut, quod nolit Marcion, parem creatoris, apud quem iustum sit adflictatoribus nostris rependi adflictationem et nobis, qui adflictemur, requietem in reuelatione domini Iesu uenientis a caelo cum angelis uirtutis suae et in flamma ignis. sed flammam et ignem delendo haereticus extinxit, ne scilicet nostratem deum faceret. lucet tamen uanitas liturae. cum enim ad ultionem uenturum scribat apostolus dominum exigendam de eis, qui deum ignorent et qui non obaudiant euangelio, quos ait poenam luituros exitialem aeternam a facie domini et a gloria ualentiae eius, sequitur, ut flammam ignis inducat, scilicet ueniens ad puniendum. ita et in hoc, nolente Marcione, crematoris dei Christus est, et in illo creatoris [est], quod etiam de ignorantibus dominum ulciscitur, id est de ethnicis. seorsum enim posuit *** euangelio non obaudientes, siue Christianos peccatores siue Iudaeos. porro de ethnicis exigere poenas, qui euangelium forte non norint, non est dei eius, qui naturaliter sit ignotus nec usquam nisi in euangelio sit reuelatus, non omnibus scibilis. creatori autem etiam naturalis agnitio debetur, ex operibus intellegendo et exinde in pleniorem notitiam requirendo. illius est ergo etiam ignorantes deum plectere, quem non liceat ignorari. ipsum quod ait: a facie domini et a gloria ualentiae eius, uerbis usus Esaiae et ex ipsa causa, eundem sapit dominum, consurgentem ut comminuat terram. Quis autem est homo delicti, filius perditionis, quem reuelari prius oportet ante domini aduentum, extollens se super omne quod deus dicitur et omnem religionem, consessurus in templo dei et deum se iactaturus? secundum nos quidem antichristus, ut docent ueteres ac nouae prophetiae, ut Iohannes apostolus, qui iam antichristos dicit processisse in mundum, praecursores antichristi spiritus, negantes Christum in carne uenisse et soluentes Iesum, scilicet in deo creatore; secundum uero Marcionem nescio, ne Christus sit creatoris. nondum (enim) uenit apud illum. quisquis est autem ex duobus, quaero, cur ueniat in omni uirtute et signis et ostentis mendacii. propterea, inquit, quod dilectionem ueritatis non susceperint, ut salui essent; et propter hoc erit eis (in) instinctum fallaciae, ut (credant mendacio, ut) iudicentur omnes, qui non crediderunt ueritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati. igitur si antichristus est secundum creatorem, deus erit creator, qui eum mittit ad impingendos eos in errorem, qui non crediderunt ueritati, ut salui fierent; eiusdem erit ueritas et salus, qui eas summissu erroris ulciscitur, id est creatoris, cui et competit zelus ipse, errore decipere quos ueritate non cepit. si uero non est antiohristus secundum nos, ergo Christus est creatoris secundum Marcionem. et quale erit, ut ad ulciscendam ueritatem suam Christum creatoris summittat? sed et (si) de antichristo consentit, proinde dixerim: quale est, ut illi satanas, angelus creatoris, sit necessarius et occidatur ab eo, habens fallaciae operatione fungi creatori? in summa, si indubitatum est eius esse et angelum et ueritatem et salutem, cuius et ira et aemulatio et fallaciae inmissio aduersus contemptores et desultores, etiam aduersus ignorantes — ut iam et Marcion de gradu cedat, deum quoque suum zeloten concedens —, quis dignius irascetur? puto qui a primordio rerum naturam operibus beneficiis plagis praedicationibus testibus ad agnitionem sui praestruxit nec tamen agnitus est, non qui semel unico euangelii instrumento, et ipso incerto nec palam alium deum praedicante, productus est. ita cui competit uindicta, ei competet materia uindictae, euangelium dico et ueritas et salus. Iubere autem operari eum, qui uelit manducare, eius disciplina est, qui boui trituranti os liberum iussit.
pass_a_gloss: We are compelled to repeat certain things over and over, so that we may confirm the coherence of these things. We say that the Lord is carried around by the apostle as the rewarder of both merits, either the creator or, what Marcion does not want, equal to the creator, with whom it is just to repay affliction to those who afflict us and to give rest to us who are afflicted, in the revelation of the Lord Jesus who comes from heaven with the angels of his power and in a flame of fire. But the heretic has deleted the flame and fire, so that he would not make our God. Nevertheless, the vanity of the erasure is evident. For when the apostle writes that the Lord will come for vengeance, to exact punishment from those who ignore God and who do not obey the gospel, who, he says, will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power, it follows that he will bring the flame of fire, namely, when he comes to punish. Thus, even against Marcion's will, Christ is the God of the creator, who also takes revenge on those who ignore the Lord, that is, the gentiles. For he has set apart those who do not obey the gospel, whether Christian sinners or Jews. Furthermore, to exact punishment from the gentiles, who perhaps do not know the gospel, is not the character of a God who is naturally unknown and is revealed nowhere except in the gospel, and is not known to all. But the creator is also due natural recognition, by understanding from his works and from there seeking fuller knowledge. Therefore, it is also the creator's role to punish those who ignore God, whom it is not lawful to ignore. The fact that he says 'from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power' uses the words of Isaiah and for the same reason, indicates the same Lord, who rises up to shake the earth. Who is the man of sin, the son of perdition, who must be revealed before the coming of the Lord, exalting himself above all that is called God and every religion, sitting in the temple of God and boasting that he is God? According to us, certainly, he is the antichrist, as the old and new prophecies teach, as the apostle John, who says that the antichrists have already come into the world, forerunners of the antichrist spirit, denying Christ came in the flesh and dissolving Jesus, namely, in the creator God; but according to Marcion, I do not know, lest Christ be the creator's. For he has not yet come according to him. Whoever he is, however, I ask, why does he come in all power and signs and lying wonders. Because, he says, they did not receive the love of truth, so that they might be saved; and because of this, there will be a delusion sent to them, so that they will believe the lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity will be judged. Therefore, if the antichrist is according to the creator, God will be the creator, who sends him to lead astray those who did not believe the truth, so that they might be saved; the truth and salvation will be of the same one, who avenges those in error, namely, the creator, to whom zeal itself is fitting, to deceive by error those whom he did not capture by truth. But if he is not the antichrist according to us, then Christ is the creator's according to Marcion. And what kind of thing is it, that the creator's Christ submits to avenge his truth? But even if he agrees about the antichrist, I will say likewise: what kind of thing is it, that Satan, the angel of the creator, is necessary to him and will be killed by him, having the operation of delusion to serve the creator? In short, if it is indisputable that the angel and truth and salvation are his, and also his wrath and emulation and the sending of delusions against despisers and mockers, and also against those who ignore him — so that Marcion may now yield, conceding that his God is also zealous — who is more worthy to be angry? I think it is the one who from the beginning of things has constructed his nature by works, benefits, blows, preachings, and witnesses for his recognition, and yet has not been recognized, not the one who has been produced once by the single instrument of the gospel, and that uncertain and not openly preaching another God. Thus, the one to whom vengeance belongs will also have the material for vengeance, namely, the gospel, truth, and salvation. Moreover, to command that one who wants to eat should work is the discipline of the one who commanded that the ox treading the grain should have its mouth free.

pass_b_english: We are forced to keep repeating certain points so that their internal coherence becomes unmistakable. The apostle presents the Lord as the rewarder of both kinds of merit, and we identify him as either the Creator or — a possibility Marcion rejects — as equal to the Creator. With this Lord it is just to pay back affliction to our afflicters and to grant rest to us who are afflicted, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus coming from heaven with the angels of his power and in a flame of fire. The heretic, however, has erased the flame and the fire so that he would not have to acknowledge our God. Yet the futility of that erasure shines through. When the apostle writes that the Lord will come to execute vengeance, exacting punishment from those who ignore God and who refuse to obey the gospel, he says they will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power (Isaiah 2:19, 21). It therefore follows that he will bring the flame of fire — precisely because he comes to punish. So even against Marcion's will, Christ is the God of the Creator who takes vengeance on those who ignore the Lord, that is, the gentiles. For the apostle has set apart those who disobey the gospel, whether they are Christian sinners or Jews. Moreover, to demand punishment from gentiles who perhaps never knew the gospel is not the character of a God who is naturally unknown and revealed nowhere except in the gospel, and not knowable by all. But the Creator is owed natural recognition — by understanding him from his works and then seeking fuller knowledge. Therefore it also belongs to the Creator to punish those who ignore God, whom it is not lawful to ignore. The phrase 'from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power' borrows the words of Isaiah and for the same reason points to the same Lord, who rises to shake the earth. Who is the man of sin, the son of perdition, who must be revealed before the Lord's coming, exalting himself above everything called God and every religion, seating himself in the temple of God and boasting that he is God (2 Thessalonians 2:4)? According to us he is certainly the antichrist, as the old and new prophecies teach, and as the apostle John teaches, who says that antichrists have already come into the world as forerunners of the antichrist spirit, denying that Christ came in the flesh and dissolving Jesus — that is, in the Creator God. But according to Marcion I do not know who he is, for fear that Christ might turn out to be the Creator's. After all, he has not yet come in Marcion's scheme. Whoever he is, I ask: why does he come in all power and signs and lying wonders? Because, the apostle says, they did not receive the love of truth so that they might be saved; and for this reason a working of delusion will be sent to them so that they will believe the lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. Therefore, if the antichrist operates according to the Creator, then God is the Creator who sends him to ensnare in error those who did not believe the truth so that they might be saved; the truth and salvation belong to the same one who avenges those led into error — namely the Creator, to whom zeal itself is fitting, deceiving by error those whom he did not capture by truth. But if he is not the antichrist according to us, then Christ is the Creator's according to Marcion. And what kind of being would he be, that the Creator's Christ submits to avenge his truth? Even if Marcion agrees about the antichrist, I will press the same question: what kind of arrangement is it that Satan, the angel of the Creator, is necessary to him and will be killed by him, exercising the operation of delusion in service to the Creator? In short, if it is indisputable that the angel, the truth, and the salvation are his, and likewise his wrath, his emulation, and his sending of delusions against despisers and mockers — and even against those who ignore him — so that Marcion must now yield ground, conceding that his own God is also zealous — who is more worthy to be angry? I think it is the one who from the beginning of things prepared his nature for recognition by works, benefits, blows, preachings, and witnesses, yet was not recognized; not the one who was produced once by the single instrument of the gospel, and that uncertain, not openly preaching another God. Thus the one to whom vengeance belongs will also possess the material for vengeance — I mean the gospel, the truth, and the salvation. Moreover, to command that the one who wants to eat should work is the discipline of the one who commanded that the ox treading out the grain should have its mouth free.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the identity of the Creator and Christ in relation to Marcion's views. Scripture citations (Isaiah and 2 Thessalonians) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Latin source.
